scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-AUTOMATABLE.statement: The dispute surge since August is driven by slow/inadequate ticket handling and correctable bill errors, both of which an AI agent can resolve by auto-answering tickets and auto-fixing bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is systematically mis-accepting or mis-rejecting reads, producing wrong bills that drive disputes.

H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery to billing (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or failed starting around August, forcing more estimate substitutions and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter-read collection/upload from the field contractor (H-FIELD-BILL) has degraded since August, increasing estimate substitutions and bill errors for manually-read accounts.

H-CORRECT-BILLS-CUSTOMER-CONFU.statement: Bills issued since August are largely accurate, and the ticket surge reflects a non-error cause (e.g., tariff/rate change or communication gap) that generates disputes without underlying billing defects.

H-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR.statement: The majority of disputed bills carry an ACTUAL read, suggesting errors in actual AMI/manual read values or their import/validation, not just estimate substitution, may be a significant driver of the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data shows median dispute-ticket response time of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets. Ticket handling speed is not an active service failure, which weakens the premise that slow response is driving the dispute surge.

billing-db's tariff_change_log has zero records, indicating no tariff or rate change was logged, which rules out a tariff/rate adjustment as the non-error explanation for the August-September dispute surge.

Of disputed bills in billing-db, 1785 involve ACTUAL reads versus 1240 ESTIMATED reads (3025 total), so a majority of disputed bills are on bills with an accepted actual read, not an estimate substitution. This weakens any explanation that pins the dispute surge mainly on estimate substitution from failed read delivery, and points toward a broader billing/import issue affecting actual reads too.

Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026, a measurable shortfall in manual meter-read collection. This explains some estimate substitution among manually-read accounts, but per E-03 most disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not ESTIMATED) reads, so this shortfall is at best a partial driver of the overall dispute surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 and 590 disputes in Jun/Jul 2026 versus 1180 and 1260 in Aug/Sep 2026, confirming the dispute surge is roughly a doubling from baseline as initially reported, but this record only quantifies the symptom's magnitude and timing and says nothing about its cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead, with authority_scope covering billing adjustments and information topic 'tariffs') states no tariff change occurred this year, corroborating E-02's billing-db tariff_change_log finding of zero logged changes. This is a stakeholder claim, not independent evidence, but it agrees with the existing authoritative tool record ruling out a tariff/rate change as the dispute-surge driver.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a staffing gap of three readers since July is causing late routes, which produces estimated (not actual) bills for the affected customers; this is an unverified stakeholder explanation for part of the E-04 route-completion shortfall, not independent evidence.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field services contract (§4.2) authoritatively confirms that the utility may request route priority changes but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, formalizing the human-approval gate already modeled as K-DISPATCH for push_route_update.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes identifies 14 specific routes with below-target completion (sample R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity for the aggregate shortfall already shown in E-04. It supplies candidate targets for a route-priority push but does not itself establish whether the field read handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded beyond the unverified staffing claim.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) shows 320 accounts billed on an estimated read last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000 on R-00). This is broader route coverage than the 14 lagging routes identified in E-09, so estimate substitution is not confined to the specific routes already tied to the staffing shortage claim, but the summary stats alone do not establish route-by-route overlap.

U-AMI-DELIVERY-CONTRIBUTION.question: Did AMI/MDMS read delivery (H-MDMS-BILL) degrade since August, contributing to wrong actual-read bills (H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE)?

U-FIELD-HANDOFF-DEGRADATION.question: Beyond the claimed staffing shortage (E-07, unverified stakeholder claim), has the field manual-read handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) itself degraded in delivery or semantic validity?
U-FIELD-HANDOFF-DEGRADATION.decision_impact: If the handoff itself (not just staffing) has degraded, the remedy may require process fixes with ORG-FIELD in addition to any route-priority change SH-FIELD requests.
U-FIELD-HANDOFF-DEGRADATION.resolution_path: Run analyze_field_read_handoff against H-FIELD-BILL to check delivery_status and semantic_validity independent of SH-FIELD's unverified staffing claim.
U-FIELD-HANDOFF-DEGRADATION.safe_placeholder: Keep push_route_update gated behind SH-FIELD's runtime confirmation (K-DISPATCH) regardless of this unknown's outcome.

U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-SUCCESS-PR.resolution_path: Track the actual_read_dispute_share metric alongside dispute_volume and audit a sample of resolved disputes to confirm root-cause closure rather than relying on ticket count alone.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-AS-SUCCESS-PR.safe_placeholder: Report dispute_volume trend together with actual_read_dispute_share; do not treat volume decline alone as proof of fixed bills.
